title: Under true concurrency, a stale --if-revision with a gone removal target still exits 6, not 5
description: Reported by lore-cli 2026-09-27 and filed on opum-agent's instruction, targeted at the NEXT pair version, not 0.11.0 (ruling: v0.11.0 at eb1d9f4 stands, and lore LCLI-614 absorbs this for the pair). MEASURED by lore-cli against the v0.11.0 darwin-arm64 build (run 36285769701, sha256 d6a10b42). SERIAL: quest task edit <id> --remove-label x --if-revision <stale> after a competing removal exits 5 conflict (the QCLI-374 fix, also measured here, where 0.10.0 exits 6). CONCURRENT: lore unlink and a competing `quest task edit <id> --remove-label doc:<sid>` fired together. lore's argv was `task edit T-1 --actor-kind human --remove-label doc:stories/race-N --if-revision <rev read before the competitor> --json`, and it got `--remove-label: no entry matches` (validation, exit 6) in 3 of 3 manual trials. The opum-cli-e2e TASK-90 row is red 5/5 against lore c9b9377e. MECHANISM NOT YET IDENTIFIED, stated plainly: in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts the edit path reads one snapshot (prepareMutation), checks --if-revision against it (QCLI-374), builds the patch from that same snapshot, and TaskService.editOn writes with expectedRevision = snapshot.revision (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts ~1080). So a competitor committing between the read and the write should surface as a write conflict. Where the post-competitor state reaches the value check is the first thing to find: a retry or rebase in the repository write path, a revision that does not change on a label-only write, or a second read. lore-cli offered its race.sh repro. Impact: a caller that retries only on exit 5, as quest's own agent contract prescribes, cannot absorb a lost race.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mechanism is named from evidence: the code path through which a concurrent competitor's write reaches the removal value check despite a stale --if-revision
Under a real concurrent competitor, a stale --if-revision with a gone removal target exits 5 conflict, proven by a concurrency test that fails on the 0.11.0 code and passes after the fix
A current (non-stale) --if-revision with a genuinely absent target still exits 6, so the fix does not turn real misses into conflicts
opum-cli-e2e's TASK-90 row passes against this quest with a lore that does not rely on the LCLI-614 re-read

implementationNotes:
Repro and hypothesis from lore-cli, 2026-09-27 (received inline, recorded here so it outlives the session).

HYPOTHESIS (lore-cli; fits the one-snapshot path): the edit takes its snapshot BEFORE the competitor commits, so the --if-revision check passes and the patch is built against a state where the label is present. The store-level write then sees a moved revision. If anything below the command then REBUILDS the patch from a fresh snapshot (an internal retry on a store conflict, or a reload-and-reapply), the second pass finds the label gone and reports "no entry matches" without re-checking --if-revision. First place to look: any retry or reload between the precondition check and the commit.

REPRO (race.sh). Usage: PATH=<dir-with-quest>:$PATH bash race.sh <lore-wrapper> <quest> 3, where the lore wrapper is: #!/bin/sh / exec bun run /path/to/lore-cli/src/cli.ts "$@". To take lore out entirely, replace the lore unlink with a second `quest task edit $tid --remove-label doc:$sid --if-revision <rev read before the race>`. Core of each trial: git init; quest init; lore init --yes --tracker quest; sid=$(lore new story ...); tid=$(quest task create ...); lore link $sid $tid; then in parallel ( lore unlink $sid $tid ) & ( quest task edit $tid --remove-label doc:$sid ) &; wait; compare exit codes and the labels afterwards. lore-cli observed lore exit 6 "no entry matches" in 3 of 3 against the v0.11.0 build (sha256 d6a10b42).
finalSummary:
RETIRED: no defect. The report that prompted this task was withdrawn by its author, and a quest-only measurement here confirms the withdrawal independently.

WITHDRAWN (lore-cli, 2026-09-27): the LCLI-614 implementer instrumented a real race. The revision lore sent was EQUAL to the record's, so nothing raced at quest's level. lore's read landed after the competitor removed the label, and lore then sent --remove-label unconditionally with a CURRENT revision. Removing an absent label is a genuine validation miss, so quest's exit 6 was correct. The mistake was reading "--if-revision was sent" as "the revision was stale" without comparing it with the record's.

MEASURED HERE, not taken on the withdrawal: a quest-only race over 20 trials per build, each in a disposable workspace. Two `quest task edit T-1 --remove-label x --if-revision <same pre-race revision>` were launched in parallel. Results: 0.11.0 (v0.11.0 build, sha256 d6a10b42) had one exit 0 and one exit 5 in 20/20. 0.10.0 (installed) also had one exit 0 and one exit 5 in 20/20. The 0.10.0 row is the positive control that the edits truly overlapped: run in sequence, 0.10.0's known serial defect gives 6, and the serial repro earlier today measured 0.10.0 = 6 and 0.11.0 = 5. So under true concurrency the loser gets the write-time expectedRevision conflict (exit 5) on both builds. The only exit-6 path for a stale --if-revision was 0.10.0's serial one, which QCLI-374 fixed in 0.11.0.

No acceptance criterion is checked, because none describes a real defect. Archived rather than completed, so no one reads it as delivered work.
